headline: AP calls Ohio and Texas Senate races for Democrats Sherrod Brown and James Talarico, and Iowa governor for Rob Sand
body: The Associated Press has called two more Senate seats that are currently held by Republicans for Democratic candidates, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown wins against Republican Jon Husted, with the tracker showing Brown on 48.6% to Husted's 46.5% with about 87% of the expected vote counted. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico wins against Republican Ken Paxton, 59.2% to 39.2% with about 67% counted. That makes four Senate seats called for a different party tonight, after North Carolina and South Carolina. AP has also called Oregon for Democratic incumbent Jeff Merkley. Senate calls now stand at 21: 15 for Democrats and 6 for Republicans. In the House, AP has called Ohio's 15th district for Democrat Don Leonard over Republican incumbent Mike Carey (52.2% to 45.0%, about 97% counted), the seventh House seat called for a different party so far. The tracker shows 232 House races called: 139 for Democrats and 93 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. In the governor races, AP has called Iowa for Democrat Rob Sand, who leads Republican Zach Lahn 57.4% to 42.6% with about 82% counted; the governorship is currently held by Republicans. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

headline: AP calls South Carolina Senate for Democrat Annie Andrews over Lindsey Graham, and Ohio governor for Amy Acton
body: The Associated Press has called South Carolina's Senate race for Democrat Annie Andrews over Republican incumbent Lindsey Graham, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. The tracker shows Andrews on 50.6% to Graham's 47.2% with about 93% of the expected vote counted. It is the second Senate seat called for a different party tonight, after North Carolina. AP has also called Arkansas for Republican incumbent Tom Cotton, who has 54.6% with about 84% counted. Senate calls now stand at 18: 12 for Democrats and 6 for Republicans. In the House, AP has called two more Republican-held Pennsylvania seats for Democrats: Paige Cognetti wins the 8th district over incumbent Rob Bresnahan (55.2% to 44.8%, about 94% counted), and Janelle Stelson wins the 10th over incumbent Scott Perry (55.5% to 44.5%, about 97% counted). That makes six House seats called for a different party so far. The tracker shows 201 House races called: 127 for Democrats and 74 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. AP has also called Louisiana's 4th district for House Speaker Mike Johnson. In the governor races, AP has called Ohio for Democrat Amy Acton, who leads Republican Vivek Ramaswamy 50.7% to 46.0% with about 85% counted; the governorship is currently held by Republicans. AP has also called Arkansas for Republican Sarah Huckabee Sanders and New Mexico for Democrat Deb Haaland. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

headline: AP calls two more House seats for Democrats in Kentucky and Pennsylvania, and Georgia's governor race for Keisha Lance Bottoms
body: The Associated Press has called two more House seats that are currently held by Republicans for Democratic candidates, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. In Kentucky's 6th district, Democrat Zach Dembo wins, with the tracker showing him on 52.7% to Republican Ralph Alvarado's 43.3% with about 99% of the expected vote counted. In Pennsylvania's 7th district, Democrat Bob Brooks wins against Republican incumbent Ryan Mackenzie, on 56.6% to 43.4% with about 78% counted. That makes four House seats called for a different party so far, after North Carolina's 11th and New Jersey's 7th. The tracker now shows 182 House races called: 116 for Democrats and 66 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. In the governor races, AP has called Georgia for Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, who leads Republican Rick Jackson 54.2% to 45.8% with about 86% counted; the governorship is currently held by Republicans. There have been no new Senate calls since our last update, so Senate calls stay at 16: 11 for Democrats and 5 for Republicans. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

body: The Associated Press has called New Jersey's 7th congressional district for Democrat Rebecca Bennett, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. headline: AP calls Senate races in Kentucky and Oklahoma for Republicans; House calls pass 130
body: The Associated Press has called two more Senate races for Republicans, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. In Kentucky, Republican Andy Barr wins the seat, with the tracker showing him on 53.7% to Democrat Charles Booker's 44.2% with about 80% of the expected vote counted. In Oklahoma, Republican Kevin Hern wins, on 60.6% to Democrat N'Kiyla Thomas's 36.0% with about 59% counted. Both seats are currently held by Republicans. That brings Senate calls to 16: 11 for Democrats and 5 for Republicans, with North Carolina still the only seat to change hands. In the House, the tracker shows 135 races called: 87 for Democrats and 48 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. North Carolina's 11th district remains the only House seat called for a different party so far. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

headline: AP calls first House seat to change hands, in North Carolina's 11th district; Republicans win Senate races in Florida, West Virginia and Wyoming
body: The Associated Press has called North Carolina's 11th congressional district for Democrat Jamie Ager, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. The seat is currently held by Republicans, making it the first House seat of the night to change party. With about 88% of the expected vote counted, the tracker shows Ager on 59.0% and Republican Jennifer Balkcom on 39.6%. In the Senate, AP has called five more races: Republican holds in Florida (Ashley Moody), West Virginia (Shelley Moore Capito) and Wyoming (Harriet Hageman), and Democratic holds in Colorado (John Hickenlooper) and New Mexico (Ben Ray Luján). That brings Senate calls to 14: 11 for Democrats and 3 for Republicans, with North Carolina the only seat to change hands so far. In the House, the tracker shows 103 races called: 71 for Democrats and 32 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and neither chamber has been called.

headline: AP calls North Carolina Senate race for Roy Cooper, the first seat to change hands tonight
body: The Associated Press has called North Carolina's Senate race for Democrat Roy Cooper, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. headline: AP calls Senate races in Georgia, New Jersey, Illinois and three more states for Democrats
body: The Associated Press has called six more Senate races as Democratic holds, according to the Guardian's live results tracker, which carries AP race calls. AP called Georgia, one of the night's closely watched seats, for Jon Ossoff, and also called the races in New Jersey (Cory Booker), Illinois (Juliana Stratton), Massachusetts (Ed Markey), Delaware (Chris Coons) and Rhode Island (Jack Reed). With Virginia called earlier, that makes seven Senate calls, all Democratic holds, with no seat changing hands so far. In the House, the tracker shows 38 races called: 25 for Democrats and 13 for Republicans, with 218 needed for a majority. AP race calls are media calls, not official results; counting continues and much of the vote in many states is still to be reported. Neither chamber has been called.

headline: First race calls: Democrats hold Virginia's Senate seat; early House calls in Kentucky and Florida
body: With the first polls closed across the East, the first race calls of the night have come in. The Guardian's live results tracker, which shows Associated Press race calls, has Democrats holding the Senate seat in Virginia. In the House, it shows Democrats holding Kentucky's 3rd district and Florida's 10th, and Republicans holding Kentucky's 5th. These are media projections, not official results; state counts continue and certification comes weeks later. Neither chamber has been called. AP says control of the Senate could take days to settle and the House up to about a week, with ranked-choice tabulation possible in Alaska and Maine. Democrats need to flip four Senate seats and three House seats to win control, according to AP.
